predecessors.note: Different states despite the shared Wikidata Q139708: the French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon was the ruling power over Syria and Lebanon; Lebanon declared independence on 22 November 1943. Cliopatria's mandate row runs to 1945 and, from 1944, shows Syria alone.

capitals.note: 'Beirut is the country's capital and largest city'; designated capital of Greater Lebanon in 1920.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Lebanon row starts in 1944. The page: 'Independence declared: 22 November 1943' and the French 'released the government officials on 22 November 1943'; the mandate ended 24 October 1945 and French forces withdrew on 17 April 1946 (infobox; the text says December 1946). Cliopatria's French Mandate row still contains Lebanon in 1943.
9,810 km2 against the infobox 10,452 km2 (ratio 0.94): Greater Lebanon of 1920 ('Mount Lebanon, North Lebanon, South Lebanon, and the Bekaa'). Within the cell size of the country.

9,887 km2: two extra cells at 33.1-33.3 N, 35.5-35.6 E on the Palestine frontier (the Malkiyya-Qadas salient) that appear only in 1946-1947. Unverified: page budget; the 1948 war page has Lebanese troops crossing there on 15 May 1948.
Back to the 1944 outline. Israel's occupation of 'southern Lebanon until the end of the war' (1948 war page) is a ledger occupation, not a shape change.

The armistice line of 23 March 1949 'was drawn along the international boundary between Lebanon and Mandatory Palestine' and Israel withdrew from 13 Lebanese villages, so the 1949-1966 outline is that international boundary.
No change in cells against 1949-1966; unverified: page budget (no territorial event for Lebanon in 1967 on the pages opened).
One extra cell at 33.85 N, 35.54 E on the Beirut coast, 1973-1975 only; noise.

Back to the 1944 outline for 1976-1982. Syria's army entered on 31 May 1976 ('Syria occupies northern and eastern Lebanon'); Israel's invasion of March 1978 held a border strip. Both are ledger occupations; Cliopatria's shape does not show them.

region.text: the regions of Mount Lebanon, North Lebanon, South Lebanon and the Bekaa, with Beirut as capital

ledger.note: 22 November 1943: Lebanon declares independence from France. Infobox 'Independence declared: 22 November 1943'; Greater Lebanon had been established on 1 September 1920 and the constitution adopted on 23 May 1926; the French mandate ended on 24 October 1945 and French forces withdrew on 17 April 1946 (the text: 'December 1946').

region.text: southern Lebanon, which Israel 'invaded and occupied ... until the end of the war': the '13 villages in Lebanese territory, which were occupied during the war', drawn as the border strip two cells deep

ledger.note: 1948: Israel occupies southern Lebanon. 'Israel then invaded and occupied southern Lebanon until the end of the war.' The page gives no month for the occupation. Reviewer me-10-i (2026-10-25): region narrowed from the South Lebanon and Nabatiyeh governorates (about 2,000 km2) to the border strip: the armistice page names only the 13 villages Israel left, and neither page names the Awali or the Litani.

region.text: northern Galilee, where a token Lebanese force crossed on 15 May 1948 and seized two villages (al-Malkiyya and Qadas were retaken on 5-6 June)

ledger.note: 15 May 1948: Lebanon enters the war. 'On 15 May, the 2nd Yarmuk Battalion crossed the border' and a 'token force of 436 soldiers' of the Lebanese Army crossed into northern Galilee, seized two villages and withdrew; Israel retook al-Malkiyya on 28-29 May and Lebanon recaptured it and Qadas on 5-6 June; Lebanon withdrew 'on 8 July'.

region.text: southern Lebanon, which Israel 'invaded and occupied ... until the end of the war': the '13 villages in Lebanese territory, which were occupied during the war', drawn as the border strip two cells deep

ledger.note: 23 March 1949: Israel leaves Lebanese territory. The armistice 'was drawn along the international boundary between Lebanon and Mandatory Palestine' and 'Israel withdrew its forces from 13 villages in Lebanese territory, which were occupied during the war.' Reviewer me-10-i (2026-10-25): region narrowed from the South Lebanon and Nabatiyeh governorates (about 2,000 km2) to the border strip: the armistice page names only the 13 villages Israel left, and neither page names the Awali or the Litani.

region.text: northern Galilee, where a token Lebanese force crossed on 15 May 1948 and seized two villages (al-Malkiyya and Qadas were retaken on 5-6 June)

ledger.note: 23 March 1949: Lebanon and Israel sign the armistice (Syria signed on 20 July 1949), ending the fighting along the frontier.

31 May 1976: the Syrian army enters Lebanon. 'On May 31, 1976, the Syrian Army invaded Lebanon with 2,000 troops and 60 tanks'; infobox 'Syria occupies northern and eastern Lebanon'; the enlarged Arab Deterrent Force, mostly Syrian, gave it Arab League cover (October 1976, Lebanon page). The region is the page's 'northern and eastern' read as the Beqaa and North Lebanon governorates; on 13 October 1990 Syrian forces 'attacked and occupied the Presidential Palace at Baabda', which widens the hold, but the page does not give its extent.

region.text: the border strip of South Lebanon, the 'security zone' 19 kilometres wide, drawn as two cells (about 18 km) from the frontier

ledger.note: March 1978: Israel invades south Lebanon. 'On 11 March 1978 ... Israel invaded Lebanon four days later and occupied most of the area south of the Litani River'; UN Resolution 425 created UNIFIL; 'Israeli forces withdrew later in 1978, but retained control of the southern region' through a security zone. The page gives no month for the withdrawal, so the ledger draws the border strip from March 1978, not the wider invasion area.

region.text: South Lebanon and Nabatiyeh governorates, the land south of the Awali and the Litani

ledger.note: 6 June 1982: Israel invades Lebanon again. The war 'began on 6 June 1982, when Israel invaded southern Lebanon', with the stated aim of pushing the PLO back 40 km.

region.text: the Chouf and the heights up to Khalde and the Beirut-Damascus road

ledger.note: June 1982: Israeli forces reach the Beirut area. The advance 'reached Khalde on 11 June' and cut the Beirut-Damascus highway; Chtaura in the Bekaa was shelled on 24 June.
14 June 1982: the siege of Beirut begins. 'The Siege of Beirut had begun on 14 June 1982'; 'More than 14,000 PLO combatants evacuated the country in August and September'.
29 September 1982: Israel leaves west Beirut. 'Israel withdrew its forces from west Beirut on 29 September, officially ending Operation Peace for Galilee.'

region.text: the Chouf and the land north of the Awali river

ledger.note: 3 September 1983: Israel withdraws south of the Awali. 'The IDF retreated south of the Awali river on 3 September 1983', amid rising guerrilla casualties; Mount Lebanon is evacuated.

ledger.note: June 1985: Israel pulls back to a security zone. 'In June 1985, the IDF unilaterally withdrew to a security zone in southern Lebanon' (completed 5 June); the South Lebanon conflict page has the phased withdrawal starting in February, 'withdrew to a security zone along the border on 29 April' and most troops leaving on 10 June 1985.

region.text: the border strip of South Lebanon, the 'security zone' 19 kilometres wide, drawn as two cells (about 18 km) from the frontier

ledger.note: 24-25 May 2000: Israel leaves Lebanon. 'On 24 May, Israel announced that it would withdraw all troops from South Lebanon'; 'All Israeli forces had withdrawn from Lebanon by the end of the next day'; on 16 June 2000 the UN Security Council 'concluded that Israel had indeed withdrawn its forces from all of Lebanon'. Lebanon still claims the Shebaa Farms.

30 April 2005: Syria completes its withdrawal. 'Syria completed its full withdrawal from Lebanon on 30 April 2005' after the Cedar Revolution that followed the assassination of Rafic Hariri (14 February 2005); Bashar al-Assad announced it on 5 March. The Lebanon page gives 'by 26 April' and 'Syria from 1976 to 2005'.

region.text: the southern border strip (about 33.15-33.41 N, 35.33-35.76 E) that Cliopatria removes from Lebanon in 2006; the page says only 'a ground invasion of Southern Lebanon'

ledger.note: 12 July 2006: Israel invades south Lebanon. 'Israel launched a ground invasion of Southern Lebanon and imposed an air-and-naval blockade'; the ceasefire took effect at 8:00 am on 14 August. The page does not say how far the troops went; the region is the southern strip Cliopatria removes from 2006.

ledger.note: 1 October 2006: Israel withdraws from Lebanon except Ghajar. 'On 1 October, most Israeli troops withdrew from Lebanon.'
October 2006: Israel keeps Ghajar. The last troops 'continued to occupy the border-straddling village of Ghajar'; infobox 'Israel occupies Ghajar until present'. No end within the data.

region.text: the border villages of South Lebanon where the IDF operated (Kafr Kila, Ayta ash Shab, Meiss Ej Jabal; 'They briefly captured a hill in Chamaa'), drawn as the border strip one cell deep

ledger.note: 1 October 2024: Israel invades Lebanon. 'On 1 October 2024, Lebanon was invaded by Israel.' A ceasefire was signed in November 2024 after '13 months of conflict': 'Hezbollah was given 60 days to end its armed presence in southern Lebanon and Israeli forces were obliged to withdraw from the area over the same period'. The page does not say whether they left, so no end is recorded. Reviewer me-10-i (2026-10-25): region narrowed from the South Lebanon and Nabatiyeh governorates to the border strip, after the 2024 invasion page (villages on the frontier; the ceasefire took effect on 27 November 2024 and Israeli forces 'were to withdraw from Lebanon by 26 January 2025'), which is now its source.

wars.outcome: 'A full-scale civil war broke out in Lebanon'; it 'ended at the end of 1990 after 16 years'. Syria's army entered on 31 May 1976 and stayed until 2005; the Taif Agreement of September 1989 set an outline timetable for Syrian withdrawal.
wars.note: The page does not date the outbreak beyond 1975 in the sentences read; the Arab Deterrent Force dates from October 1976.

notes: One state or two: Wikidata Q139708 is shared with french-mandate-for-syria-and-lebanon, but they are different states. The mandate was France's rule over Syria and Lebanon (1920-1945 in Cliopatria; its 1944-1945 shape is already Syria alone); Lebanon is the independent republic that declared independence on 22 November 1943. This dossier therefore stays separate, starts in November 1943 (Cliopatria: 1944; a new keyframe covers 1943) and names the mandate as predecessor; the mandate dossier should hand Lebanon over in 1943. Cliopatria's removals of the south in 1983-1986 and 2006-2013 are corrected to ledger occupations (land stays Lebanese). The 1987-2005 shape already keeps the whole country. The Israeli border-strip region uses a border_band between lebanon and state-of-israel with width 2 cells; that needs both shapes to exist in 1990 (they do). Needs another dossier: the Israeli-backed Free Lebanon State and the South Lebanon provisional administration, 'South Lebanon Security Belt' (the page names them; years not read), which held the security zone; Palestinian bases in south Lebanon (not read). Not read within the five-page budget: the 1958 insurrection (the Lebanon page gives one sentence), the Taif Agreement text (September 1989), the 1949-1966 and 1967 Syrian and Israeli frontier incidents, the Syrian civil war spillover (Arsal, 2014), the Lebanon-Syria border demarcation. The 1982 page and the Lebanon page disagree on the French withdrawal (17 April 1946 infobox, December 1946 text) and the Lebanon page gives 26 April 2005 for the Syrian withdrawal against 30 April on the occupation page. Gazetteer names needed: Ghajar (village on the Lebanon-Israel-Syria tripoint, here a 5 km radius around 35.62 E 33.28 N from my own reading, not a page) and Shebaa Farms (not used in a region).
